target_customer: Consumers buying greeting cards, notebooks and wrapping paper; freelance designers as suppliers
problem: Mass-market paper goods (led by Hallmark) offered limited design variety and did not take outside designers' work; Chirply let a community submit and vote on designs and then produced the winners.
business_model: Marketplace/manufacturer: cards sold at $4 each or $25 for a set of 10, designers paid a $300 prize plus 10 cents per printed item

founders.name: Neel Palrecha
founders.background_notes: Brother of Gagan; no bio on YC page.

competitors.name: Hallmark
competitors.what: Industry leader in greeting cards; did not accept unsolicited artwork
competitors.traction_then: Spent about $60M a year on card designs (ReadWrite)

competitors.name: Papyrus
competitors.what: Premium greeting cards, $6 to $10 per card

competitors.name: Minted
competitors.what: Design-community marketplace specializing in bulk greeting cards

technical_complexity.rationale: Web community with voting plus outsourced print production; operational (print fulfilment) more than technical.

defensibility.rationale: Only a possible designer and voter community; Threadless-style model could be copied, and Threadless later partnered on greeting cards (2013-14).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Threadless entered greeting cards via Open Me (2013) and Recycled Paper Greetings (2014); no source shows anyone acquiring Chirply.

market_need_then: TechCrunch called paper goods a relatively open space; Chirply reported about 200,000 pageviews and over 100 design submissions since a February 2011 soft launch and made first designer payments.

identity.voice_and_tone: Community-design positioning ('crowd-sourced and crowd-curated design community for paper goods')

branding.brand_signature: Positioned as Threadless for paper goods
branding.community_and_virality: Designer interview blog on the April 2011 relaunch; coverage in TechCrunch, ReadWrite, VentureBeat, Xconomy and a mom-blog review; no evidence of merch or fan accounts.

brand_strength.rationale: Some launch press and a clear 'Threadless for X' pitch, but no evidence of lasting recognition or community.

pivots.from: Original idea not identified in sources
pivots.why: Pivot reported about a month before YC S10 demo day; reason not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Chirply pivoted shortly before demo day into a Threadless-style marketplace for greeting cards, soft-launched in February 2011 and raised $1.1M in April 2011 from well-known angels, YC and Founder Collective. YC lists it Inactive (CB Insights and Dealroom say dead or closed) but no shutdown announcement, date or cause was found, so the cause is not public.
notes: Cause and date of shutdown not public; status inferred from YC Inactive plus aggregators. Investor lists differ by source (TechCrunch used here; CB Insights, Startupintros list others); total $1.12M per CB Insights agrees with $1.1M. Competitors are dated April 2011 (launch coverage), about 8 months after the S10 batch, since no earlier dated sources found. chirply.com did not resolve from this session (network); site status unknown. Name origin, logo and mascot not found. Founded year not stated by YC.
